events.extended_summary: Amid growing speculation that Iran could attempt to break the US' naval blockade of its ports, MarineTraffic data appeared to show an Iranian tanker called "Khat-Shekan" sailing through the Strait of Hormuz. However, the tanker-tracking site TankerTrackers has said it was a "spoof" and that the vessel does not exist. "All of the data supplementing that AIS transmission is wrong and there's nothing on satellite imagery to corroborate those movements," TankerTrackers said in a post on social media, adding that the "Iranians know better than to attempt to ship out a VLCC right now given how many were fired upon in recent months." The reported movement came as satellite images and ship-tracking data published in recent days showed more than 14 oil tankers had gathered around Kharg Island, a key Iranian export terminal. events.micro_summary: Tracker says Iranian tanker reported in Strait of Hormuz is fake.
events.summary: Tracker says Iranian tanker reported in Strait of Hormuz is fake.

events.extended_summary: Leading AI laboratories face mounting scrutiny over safety governance and economic disruption. Safety researchers have recently resigned from OpenAI and Anthropic, warning that commercial pressures override safety guardrails and that corporate structures operate like autocracies. Meanwhile, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has warned that AI will soon surpass humans at nearly all tasks, temporarily leaving physical-world jobs as the only human advantage before becoming obsolete. He argued that current economic systems will no longer make sense, necessitating broader societal conversations about reorganizing the economy, possibly through universal income or a capitalist system of AI agents distributing resources. As policymakers, tech workers, and international experts gather in London to discuss AI safety, critics emphasize that external regulation cannot succeed if companies remain internally undemocratic.
events.micro_summary: AI labs face safety resignations and economic warnings as experts gather in London to address governance.
events.summary: Safety researchers quit major AI labs citing broken safety cultures, while Anthropic's CEO warns advanced AI will upend economies, as global experts gather in London to address AI safety governance.

events.extended_summary: Donald Trump described Vladimir Putin as his 'friend' during a meeting in China and in a social media post, prompting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to state that Putin is a 'killer' and an 'enemy' to Ukraine. The remarks came as Russian missile and drone strikes killed at least 11 people across Ukraine, including two in Kryvyi Rih and nine in Kyiv and western regions in an attack Zelensky called the 'biggest this year' involving 110 missiles and over 400 drones. In the UK, Reform deputy leader Richard Tice called Putin a 'murderous dictator' and expressed 'horror' at Trump's comments, while Conservative deputy Alex Burghart said he was 'very sad' about the post. Poland also reported a Russian cruise missile violated its airspace. Polling found only 10% of British people hold a favourable view of Trump.
events.micro_summary: Donald Trump called Vladimir Putin his friend, prompting Zelensky to call the Russian leader a killer.
events.summary: Trump called Putin his 'friend' in China, prompting Zelensky to call him a 'killer' while UK's Reform and Conservatives condemned the remarks amid Russian strikes that killed at least 11.

events.extended_summary: Finland says work is continuing on the Sparta II ship on Sunday Rescue and firefighting efforts are continuing for a Russian cargo vessel hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, authorities have said. The ship - the Sparta II - was bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday that work was ongoing to make sure the cargo ship did not sink but it was not aware of any danger to surrounding maritime traffic. Water was still being used to douse the ship on Sunday, and Finland said Estonian and Russian assets were also involved in recovery work. events.extended_summary: Close to 200 countries meeting in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual UN climate summit COP31 failed to finalize a cover decision mentioning fossil fuels, known as the Antalya pact. A coalition of about 130 parties, including the EU, UK, and scores of developing nations, demanded recognition of the need to transition away from fossil fuels, but their demands failed. All countries had previously agreed to this transition at COP28 in Dubai in 2023. Many developing nations prioritized finance over fossil fuel language, facing debt crises and extreme weather impacts. At COP29 in Baku in 2024, rich countries pledged $300 billion annually by 2035 from public sources and facilitated $1 trillion in private funding.
events.micro_summary: COP31 climate summit in Antalya failed to include fossil fuel transition language despite 130 countries demanding it.
events.summary: Nearly 200 countries at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya failed to agree on a final pact mentioning fossil fuels, despite a coalition of about 130 nations demanding a transition away from them.

events.extended_summary: United Nations climate talks (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, approached a final deal as negotiations extended into overtime past a Friday deadline. President Murat Kurum said a text had been put forward that all parties could agree upon, with delegations given until 3am GMT to raise objections before a 6am GMT session. Co-led by Australia's Chris Bowen and hosted by Turkey, the conference involved nearly 200 delegations. Civil society warned that developed countries blocked progress without new finance commitments, abandoning the Global South. The draft lacked references to ending fossil fuels, though Kurum said concerns were addressed. At a side event, the Landscape Alliance promoted an integrated approach addressing climate, biodiversity and land degradation, citing Indonesia's Sungsang IV village where mangrove restoration supports livelihoods and carbon storage. The talks followed climate disasters including Mozambique floods that damaged over 150,000 homes and killed at least 22 people.
events.micro_summary: UN climate talks in Turkey approach final deal after overtime negotiations.

sources.publisher: Forests News, Center for International Forestry Research

events.summary: UN climate talks (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, approached a final consensus deal after running into overtime, with negotiators working past deadlines amid concerns over fossil fuel references and climate finance for developing nations.

events.extended_summary: Iran's army stated that on Friday evening, its air defense systems detected and fired a missile at a US F-16 fighter jet flying over the Strait of Hormuz, claiming the missile exploded near the aircraft, damaged it, and forced an emergency landing. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps also claimed responsibility for targeting the jet. However, United States Central Command denied these allegations on Saturday, stating the claim that Iran targeted and damaged a US F-16 is false and that Iran did not attack any US fighter aircraft at all. CENTCOM confirmed that all US military fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for. The conflicting claims emerged amid rising regional tensions, with reports that Israel and the United States are considering renewed military action against Iran.
events.micro_summary: US Central Command denied Iran's claim of hitting an F-16 fighter jet with a missile.
events.summary: Iran claimed its air defense fired a missile at a US F-16 over the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, damaging it and forcing an emergency landing, but US Central Command denied the attack, stating all jets are safe.

events.extended_summary: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix, holding off Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in a chaotic race featuring 35 lead changes. Piastri started from 17th position and gained 14 places to secure third, his first podium since Miami in May. Verstappen's victory marked his fourth win in six races and his third Las Vegas triumph in four years. George Russell crashed at turn five on the penultimate lap, while Kimi Antonelli lost power on the final lap. Both Ferrari drivers received 10-second penalties, with Charles Leclerc penalized for spinning teammate Lewis Hamilton and Hamilton punished for leaving the track and gaining an advantage against Norris.
events.micro_summary: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
events.summary: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in a race with 35 lead changes. Piastri started 17th and gained 14 places, while George Russell crashed late and Ferrari drivers received penalties.

events.extended_summary: The contrast between Manchester United's Class of 92 and Liverpool's 1990s "Spice Boys" remains stark, with United players winning 50 Premier League medals to Liverpool's zero. Under manager Roy Evans, Liverpool's side won only the 1994-95 League Cup in four full seasons, despite playing exciting football. Robbie Fowler defended the era, noting it produced some of his best football, though acknowledging misbehavior. Neil Ruddock recalled a dressing-room mantra of "Win, draw or lose, first to the bar for booze," while the team wore white suits at Wembley. The "Spice Boys" label persists as a cautionary tale of wasted talent and excess, contrasting with United's sustained success.
events.micro_summary: Liverpool's Spice Boys won only the 1994-95 League Cup while Manchester United's Class of 92 won 50 Premier League medals.
events.summary: Liverpool's 1990s 'Spice Boys' won only the 1994-95 League Cup in four seasons under Roy Evans, contrasting with Manchester United's Class of 92, who won 50 Premier League medals to Liverpool's zero, amid stories of excess and underachievement.

events.extended_summary: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole position after a chaotic 50-lap race on the Las Vegas Strip Circuit featuring 34 changes of the lead and 352 total overtakes. The Red Bull driver withstood extreme pressure from George Russell and newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli, retaking the lead multiple times after being passed on the long straights. With two laps remaining, Russell crashed into a barrier while attempting to pass team-mate Antonelli for second place. On the final lap, Antonelli made a deployment error that allowed Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to secure a double podium for McLaren. Verstappen described the race as crazy and surreal, noting the slipstream made it impossible to pull clear. This victory marked Verstappen's third win in four Las Vegas Grands Prix.
events.micro_summary: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix after 34 lead changes and over 300 overtakes in 50 laps.
events.summary: Max Verstappen won a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix with 34 lead changes and 352 overtakes in 50 laps, as George Russell crashed with two laps remaining and McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri secured a double podium.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government. It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged. events.extended_summary: Laurentiu Codin, a former inmate, claims Christian Brueckner admitted during a 2019 prison conversation near Hannover that he abducted and killed Madeleine McCann. Codin provided this information to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office in October 2024. He alleges Brueckner described entering a holiday property in Praia da Luz while searching for money and jewelry, instead finding a sleeping blonde girl. Brueckner allegedly removed the child through a ground-floor window, drove for up to 45 minutes in his campervan, sexually assaulted her, then killed her after noticing flashing police lights and panicking. Madeleine disappeared in May 2007 from the family's accommodation in Portugal shortly before her fourth birthday while her parents dined nearby. Brueckner, 49, has been the principal suspect since 2020 but has never been charged and denies involvement. Codin initially dismissed the account as boasting.
events.micro_summary: Laurentiu Codin alleges Christian Brueckner confessed to killing Madeleine McCann during 2019 prison talks.
events.summary: A former prison cellmate claims Christian Brueckner admitted abducting and killing Madeleine McCann in 2019, describing how he took the sleeping child from a Portuguese holiday apartment, drove 45 minutes, and killed her after seeing police lights.

events.extended_summary: A boat carrying passengers to a funeral capsized on Friday near Yenagoa in Bayelsa state, southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people. Two children were among the bodies recovered from the water. Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said another 24 people had been rescued and sought medical assistance. The boat operator reportedly fled the scene after passengers asked him to steer toward land, but he allegedly declined; preliminary reports suggested a mechanical problem. The boat's manager was taken into custody. Search and rescue operations were ongoing without a confirmed number of missing persons or total passengers. The Bayelsa state government urged operators and passengers to follow safety regulations, stating that overloading, speeding, recklessness and traveling without life jackets must stop.
events.micro_summary: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people.
events.summary: A boat carrying passengers to a funeral capsized near Yenagoa in Bayelsa state, Nigeria, killing at least 24 people including two children, while 24 others were rescued; the operator fled and the manager was detained.

events.extended_summary: Watch: Drone footage shows aftermath of deadly fire at Indonesian factory At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise. Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped. Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries. Rescuers recovered 24 body bags from the fire as of Sunday evening, as search operations continue to locate missing people. Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening. events.micro_summary: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory.

events.extended_summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has proposed 15 reforms across banking, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), capital markets, insurance and financial technology to strengthen India's financial system, and meet the funding requirements of a $26.5 trillion economy by 2047. Key recommendations include a permanent, rule-based liquidity window for well-governed NBFCs, a revamp of priority sector lending norms, wider investor participation in lower-rated corporate bonds, parity for NBFCs with banks in loan recovery, and a national catastrophe and climate risk pool. The proposals come as the government has constituted the High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, with a six-month mandate. The committee will examine the long-term capital requirements of banks, development finance institutions and NBFCs, review priority sector lending norms, assess prudential regulations and chart a roadmap for artificial intelligence (AI) and digital adoption. events.extended_summary: India declared their first innings at 720/9 against New Zealand on Day 4 of the first Test in Wellington, registering their third-highest total in Test cricket, their highest-ever overseas score, and the highest total by any team on New Zealand soil. The innings featured seven consecutive 50-plus partnerships—130, 165, 91, 100, 68, 75 and 54 runs—a Test record, and marked India's fifth 700-plus total. Rishabh Pant led with 128 off 153 balls, while KL Rahul scored 136, Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, Devdutt Padikkal 80, Shubman Gill 98, Dhruv Jurel 78 and Anshul Kamboj 38. New Zealand reached 119/2 at stumps, trailing by 233 runs, with Devon Conway unbeaten on 59 and Rachin Ravindra on 27.
events.micro_summary: India scored 720/9 declared against New Zealand in Wellington, recording seven consecutive 50-plus partnerships.
events.summary: India declared at 720/9 against New Zealand in Wellington on Day 4, their highest overseas Test total, with Rishabh Pant scoring 128. New Zealand reached 119/2 at stumps, trailing by 233 runs.

events.extended_summary: Seven people, including three children, were killed when a car collided head-on with a trailer truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway in Gujarat's Kutch district on Saturday night, November 21. The victims, who were from Kotdwar in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district and visiting the Rann of Kutch, belonged to three families. The deceased included soldiers Saurabh Singh Negi (30) and Rajesh Singh Rawat (32) of the 2nd Garhwal Rifles posted in Bhuj, along with their wives Savita Negi (28) and Rinki Gosai (30), and children Shivika (three months), Rakshita (eight), and Vamika (three years). The impact mangled the car completely. A three-year-old girl, Shanvi, survived as she was in a second car. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh for each deceased's family and Rs 50,000 for the injured.
events.micro_summary: Seven people, including three children, were killed in a car-truck collision in Gujarat's Kutch district on November 21.
events.summary: Seven people, including three children from Uttarakhand, died when their car collided head-on with a trailer truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway in Gujarat's Kutch district on Saturday night, November 21.
